svg.title: The maximum entropy principle as a projection
svg.desc: Left: the triangle of distributions on three outcomes with the uniform distribution at the centre and grey contour lines of equal entropy around it. A straight orange line is the sheet of all distributions with a prescribed average. It touches one entropy contour at a single point, the maximum-entropy distribution, which is the foot of the blue curve from the uniform distribution; the blue curve is the exponential family that collects the maximum-entropy points for all prescribed averages. Right: the entropy along the sheet rises to a single peak at the maximum-entropy point.
svg.text: one peak, where the sheet touches a contour
orange: the sheet M(a) of distributions with the prescribed average; blue: the family of max-entropy points for all averages
D(P : P₀) = D(P : P̂) + D(P̂ : P₀) for every P on the sheet, so P̂ is the closest to uniform
